Nola
Nola is a 2003 American romantic comedy film written and directed by Alan Hruska. It depicts the struggle of a young woman trying to survive in New York City while looking for her birth father. It premiered in New York City on July 23, 2004.

Alan Hruska
Writer and director of Nola.

New York City
City where Nola premiered on July 23, 2004, and where the film depicts a young woman trying to survive.
City where the Society was originally incorporated in 1926; Central Park is in New York City; 23rd Street ferry boats were to New York City.
City where Great Eastern shows filled a gap and where Great Eastern hosted two shows annually from 1993–1995.
International city where Mick Batyske has performed.

romantic comedy
Genre of Nola, described as a 2003 American romantic comedy film.

birth father
The person the young woman in Nola is looking for.

Shinee
South Korean boy group that received several awards and nominations for their music work.

S.M. Entertainment
Company that formed Shinee in 2008.

The Shinee World
Shinee's first full-length album, released on August 28, 2008; it won Newcomer Album of the Year at the 23rd Golden Disk Awards.

Newcomer Album of the Year
Award won by The Shinee World at the 23rd Golden Disk Awards.

23rd Golden Disk Awards
Awards event where The Shinee World won Newcomer Album of the Year.

Sanso Gateun Neo (Love Like Oxygen)
First single released from The Shinee World; it won first place on M Countdown on September 18, 2008, Shinee's first win on Korean music shows since debut.

M Countdown
Korean music show where Sanso Gateun Neo (Love Like Oxygen) won first place on September 18, 2008.

Lucifer
Shinee's second album from 2010; it produced two singles, Lucifer and Hello, and won the Disk Bonsang Award and Popularity Award at the 25th Golden Disk Awards.

Hello
One of the two singles produced by Lucifer.

Best Dance Performance Award
Award for which Shinee was nominated at the Mnet Asian Music Awards in 2010 for outstanding choreography.

Mnet Asian Music Awards
Awards event where Shinee was nominated for Best Dance Performance Award in 2010.

Disk Bonsang Award
Award won by Lucifer at the 25th Golden Disk Awards and by Sherlock at the 27th Golden Disc Awards.

25th Golden Disk Awards
Awards event where Lucifer won the Disk Bonsang Award and the Popularity Award.

Popularity Award
Award won by Lucifer at the 25th Golden Disk Awards.

Sherlock
Shinee's fourth EP, released on March 21, 2012; it was awarded another Disk Bonsang Award at the 27th Golden Disc Awards and the Bonsang Award at the 22nd Seoul Music Award.

27th Golden Disc Awards
Awards event where Sherlock was awarded another Disk Bonsang Award.

Bonsang Award
Award awarded to Sherlock at the 22nd Seoul Music Award.

22nd Seoul Music Award
Awards event where Sherlock received the Bonsang Award.

Song of the Year
Award for which the lead single was nominated at the 2012 Mnet Asian Music Awards.

2012 Mnet Asian Music Awards
Awards event where the lead single was nominated for Song of the Year.

lead single
Following its success, it was nominated for Song of the Year at the 2012 Mnet Asian Music Awards.

Loan modification
Systematic alteration of mortgage loan agreements to help borrowers having problems making payments by reducing interest rates, monthly payments or principal balances; practiced in the United States since the 2008 Crash of the Housing Market and became national policy during the Great Recession.

Mortgage loan agreements
Mortgage agreements altered by loan modification; terms can be altered to prevent economic destabilization.

Borrowers
People having problems making mortgage payments; lending institutions' changes can relieve their financial pressure and prevent foreclosure.

Foreclosure
Condition that loan modifications and lending institution changes aim to prevent.

United States
Country where loan modifications have been practiced since the 2008 Crash of the Housing Market; HAMP TEAMS went across it.
Country whose politics form the basis of the album's concept.

2008 Crash of the Housing Market
Housing market crash since which loan modifications have been practiced in the United States.

Washington Mutual
Institution named in connection with loan modifications practiced since the 2008 Crash of the Housing Market.

Chase Home Finance
Institution named in connection with loan modifications practiced since the 2008 Crash of the Housing Market.

Chase
Institution named in connection with loan modifications practiced since the 2008 Crash of the Housing Market.

JP Morgan & Chase
Institution named in connection with loan modifications practiced since the 2008 Crash of the Housing Market.

MER's
Other contributor named in connection with loan modifications practiced since the 2008 Crash of the Housing Market.

United States Department of Housing
Department named in connection with modification orders and note holders' letters.

IRS
United States IRS; IRS staff introduced modification of mortgage terms and HAMP TEAMS; IRS inception of modifications is mentioned.

President Obama
President whose letters and inception are mentioned in connection with modifications and justice.

Note Holders
Holders of mortgage notes whom modifications, HMAP, HARP and HAMP aimed to help; due escrow/equity and annual or semi-annual equity checks; victims of collusion and fraud.

Modifications
Modifications birthed to help note holders, fix notes and address scams/falsifications; introduced with HARP and HAMP in 2009 to stop victimization of Note Holders.

FBI Mortgage Fraud Department
Department that came into existence.

HMAP
Birthed to help note holders get justice through reduced mortgage by making terms legal.

HARP
Introduced in 2009 with HAMP and Modifications to stop victimization of Note Holders; birthed to help note holders.

HAMP
Introduced in 2009 with HARP and Modifications to stop victimization of Note Holders.

HAMP TEAMS
Teams that went across the United States to assist homeowners victimized by predatory lending practices.

Predatory lending practices
Unethical lending practices whose victims included homeowners and consumers; actions began with the inception of balloon mortgages.

Great Depression
Event during which loan transfers, loan assumption, and loan bail out programs took place at state level to reduce foreclosures.

Federal Bureau of Investigation
Agency that responded to lending institution violations of law and came into existence as a watch dog; includes the online Computer crime division.

Federal Trade Commission
Agency that responded to lending institution violations and is named as a watch dog.

Comptroller
Official or agency responding to lending institution violations and named as a watch dog.

United States Government
Government that responded to lending institution violations; provided justice through President Obama's and IRS inception of Modifications.

State Government
State government responded to lending institution violations.

Great Recession
Early 21st-century recession during which loan modification became national policy.

Escrow
Money from note holders' payments that is rightfully theirs or homeowners'; subject of profit and modification.

Equity
Money or rights belonging to note holders; an annual or semi-annual equity check is due to the Note Holder.

Balloon mortgages
Lending product designed to make fast money off the note holder; predatory lending began with its inception and it was used to force foreclosure.

Consumer Protection Bureau
Watch dog agency named with HAMP TEAM, IRS, Comptroller, FTC, FBI, CIA, Local Police Department and ICE.

CIA
Watch dog agency named with HAMP TEAM, IRS, Comptroller, FTC Consumer Protection Bureau, FBI, Local Police Department and ICE.

Local Police Department
Watch dog agency named with HAMP TEAM, IRS, Comptroller, FTC Consumer Protection Bureau, FBI, CIA and ICE.

ICE
Watch dog agency named with HAMP TEAM, IRS, Comptroller, FTC Consumer Protection Bureau, FBI, CIA and Local Police Department.

FBI online Computer crime division
FBI division that receives and investigates computer crimes involving fraudulent documents and billing or payment changes.

Homeowners
Homeowners victimized by predatory lending; escrow is rightfully theirs; targeted by efforts to make them foreclose.

Creditors
Creditors unaware of the note holders' due annual or semi-annual equity check.

Real Estate Chain
Chain including lenders staff, attorneys, brokers and others accused of fraudulent continuation of mortgages and collusion.

State Code of Law
Source where legal action against institutions with such business practices can be viewed.

Federal Law
Source where legal action against institutions can be viewed on precedent cases available to the public.

Attorneys
Professionals in the real estate chain who claimed escrow/equity, continued fraudulent mortgages, and could unlawfully charge for modification.

Brokers
Professionals who contributed to the crash and are in the Real Estate Chain.

Lenders
Lenders who contributed to the crash and reorganized and renamed lending institutions.

Lending institutions
Institutions that make loan changes, provide mortgages, reorganize and rename, and are monitored by government agencies.

Mortgage Crash in 2008
Crash that occurred for the purpose of stealing from homeowners and obtaining monies note holders were unaware of; addressed through modifications in 2008.

Real Estate Market
Market where balloon mortgages and loans were given to staff with the expectation loan holders would default; relied on consumers' ignorance.

Consumers
Consumers who were victims of predatory lending; the market relied on their ignorance; justice for consumers is mentioned.

Loan assumptions
Method used by loan holders prior to modifications; took place during the Great Depression at state level to reduce foreclosures.

Loan transfers
Method used by loan holders prior to modifications; took place during the Great Depression at state level to reduce foreclosures.

Loan bail out programs
Programs during the Great Depression at state level to reduce levels of loan foreclosures.

Legal precedents
Precedents set through public court records; reporting agencies were created to address violations of laws to consumers.

Reporting agencies
Agencies created to address violations of laws to consumers.

Banks
Banks that ran USA Government; taking them on was described as a great and dangerous undertaking.

America
Country made Great Again as Justice for Consumers reigned.

Justice for Consumers
Outcome that reigned after taking on the banks.

Computer fraud
Illegal conduct associated with modifying terms to increase a mortgage or change the lending product to a balloon to force foreclosure.

Midwest
Region from which note holders reached out for assistance.

Democratic process
Process note holders used to seek assistance; mentioned with letters to departments.

Watch Dog agencies
Agencies such as HAMP TEAM, IRS, Comptroller, FTC Consumer Protection Bureau, FBI, CIA, Local Police Department and ICE that came into existence after the crash.

Mortgage notes
Notes fixed by Modifications to proper lower interest, escrow and tax fees; held by Note Holders.

Falsifications
Inappropriate mortgage charges, fraudulent deeds and fraudulent mortgages that Modifications addressed.

Collusion
Common practice to defraud and steal from the Note Holder; evidence as to why the Mortgage Crash in 2008 occurred.

loan holders
Loan holders experiencing crisis who used loan assumptions and loan transfers; expected to default under balloon mortgages.

IRS staff
Staff who introduced modification of mortgage terms and addressed the crisis with HAMP TEAMS.

Modification of mortgage terms
Introduced by IRS staff addressing the crisis.

2009
Year in which HARP, HAMP and Modifications were introduced.

equity check
Annual or semi-annual check due to the Note Holder.

New York Society of Model Engineers
Organization originally incorporated in 1926 in New York City; published records show it existed as early as 1905; it was formalized and incorporated under New York State laws in 1926; during the early-1950s it moved to its current location in Carlstadt, New Jersey.

NYSME
Abbreviation used for the New York Society of Model Engineers.

1926
Year the Society was originally incorporated and formalized under New York State laws.

1905
Year as early as which published records show the Society existed.

Manhattan
Area through which the organization moved to and from various locations in its early years.

gentlemen's club
Characterization of the organization in its early years as basically a gentlemen's club of members interested in all types of model building.

State of New York
State under whose laws the Society was formalized and incorporated in 1926.

Central Park
New York City park containing a lake the Society sought a permit to use for model motor boat races.

model motor boat races
Activity for which the Society sought a permit to use a lake in Central Park.

The Union Connecting
The Society's first Model Railroad, construction of which began in 1926.

WW2
War during which many Society members were called to service in the Armed Forces and the largest layout was dismantled; salvaged usable materials went into scrap drives for the War effort.

Armed Forces
Organization/service in which many Society members were called to serve during WW2.

Astor Building
Building whose basement housed the largest layout; its location was requested for the war effort and the layout was dismantled with care.

Lackawanna Railroad
Railroad that invited the Society to move into its Passenger Terminal in Hoboken, NJ; the Society's layout was based on the Lackawanna Railroad from Hoboken to Scranton, Pa.

Passenger Terminal in Hoboken, NJ
Lackawanna Railroad passenger terminal in Hoboken, NJ, into which the Society was invited to move; the railroad had space there for what would become the largest model railroad in the world at that time.

Hoboken
New Jersey city where the Lackawanna Railroad Passenger Terminal was located; the Society's layout route ran from Hoboken to Scranton, Pa.

ferry boats to 23rd Street
Recently discontinued ferry boats to 23rd Street in New York City; their ornate waiting room was the space in the terminal for the layout.

23rd Street
New York City street to which recently discontinued ferry boats ran; their waiting room became the layout space.

Scranton, Pa.
Destination of the Lackawanna Railroad route on which the Society's layout was based.

Hoboken Terminal
Terminal represented by a scale model in the Society's layout.

Delaware Water Gap
Landmark featured in the Society's layout, described as soaring.

Carlstadt, New Jersey
Current location of the organization after it moved there during the early-1950s.

early-1950s
Time during which the organization moved to its current location in Carlstadt, New Jersey.

largest model railroad in the world
What the Society's layout in the Lackawanna Railroad Passenger Terminal would become at that time.

Esma Sultan
Esma Sultan (21 March 1873 – 7 May 1899) was an Ottoman princess, the daughter of Sultan Abdülaziz and his wife Gevheri Kadın, and the half-sister of Abdülmecid II.
Original owner of the Esma Sultan Mansion, after whom the mansion is named.
Child of Gevheri Kadın and described as of the Ottoman Empire.

Ottoman princess
Status or role of Esma Sultan, who was an Ottoman princess.

Sultan Abdülaziz
Ottoman sultan; father of Esma Sultan and husband of Gevheri Kadın.

Gevheri Kadın
Wife of Sultan Abdülaziz and mother of Esma Sultan; daughter of Salih Bey Svatnba.
Gevheri Kadın (8 July 1856 – 6 September 1884) was the fifth wife of 32nd Ottoman Sultan Abdülaziz and the mother of Şehzade Mehmed Seyfeddin and Esma Sultan.

Salih Bey Svatnba
Father of Gevheri Kadın.

Abdülmecid II
Half-brother of Esma Sultan and the last Caliph of the Muslim world.

Caliph of the Muslim world
Role held by Abdülmecid II, described as the last Caliph of the Muslim world.

Big Stone Gap (film)
2014 American drama romantic comedy film written and directed by Adriana Trigiani and produced by Donna Gigliotti for Altar Identity Studios; based on Trigiani's 2000 best-selling novel of the same name; story set in the actual Virginia town of Big Stone Gap circa 1970s; had its world premiere at the Virginia Film Festival on November 6, 2014.

Adriana Trigiani
Wrote and directed Big Stone Gap; author of the 2000 best-selling novel of the same name.

Donna Gigliotti
Producer of Big Stone Gap for Altar Identity Studios.

Altar Identity Studios
Studio for which Donna Gigliotti produced Big Stone Gap; a subsidiary of Media Society.

Media Society
Parent company of Altar Identity Studios.

Trigiani's 2000 best-selling novel of the same name
Trigiani's 2000 best-selling novel of the same name, on which Big Stone Gap is based.

Big Stone Gap (town)
Actual Virginia town where the film's story is set, circa 1970s.

Virginia
State containing the town of Big Stone Gap.

Virginia Film Festival
Festival where Big Stone Gap had its world premiere on November 6, 2014.

November 6, 2014
Date of the film's world premiere at the Virginia Film Festival.

drama romantic comedy
Genre of Big Stone Gap (film); the film is described as an American drama romantic comedy film.

1970s
Period in which the film's story is set, circa 1970s.

Conrad Brooks
American actor born Conrad Biedrzycki on January 3, 1931 in Baltimore, Maryland; moved to Hollywood, California in 1948 to pursue acting; appeared in Ed Wood films such as "Plan 9 from Outer Space", "Glen or Glenda", and "Jail Bait"; took a break from acting during the 1960s and 1970s; reemerged in the 1980s and became a prolific actor; has since written, produced, and directed several films.

Conrad Biedrzycki
Conrad Brooks's birth name.

Baltimore
City in Maryland where Conrad Brooks was born.

Maryland
State named as part of Conrad Brooks's birthplace, Baltimore, Maryland.

Hollywood
California location to which Conrad Brooks moved in 1948.
Place where Craft entered the film industry in 1927.

California
State where Hollywood is located and where Conrad Brooks moved in 1948.
State where Craft died in Los Angeles.

Ed Wood
Filmmaker whose films Conrad Brooks appeared in; ongoing interest in his films is cited as the reason for Brooks's 1980s reemergence.
Cult filmmaker portrayed by Johnny Depp in Ed Wood (film); the film concerns a period in his life when he made his best-known films and his relationship with Bela Lugosi.

Plan 9 from Outer Space

Glen or Glenda
Ed Wood film in which Conrad Brooks appeared.

Jail Bait
Ed Wood film in which Conrad Brooks appeared.

actor

acting
Career/activity Conrad Brooks pursued and later took a break from.

January 3, 1931
Conrad Brooks's birth date.

1948
Year Conrad Brooks moved to Hollywood, California.

1980s
Period in which Conrad Brooks reemerged as a prolific actor.

films
Several films that Conrad Brooks has written, produced, and directed.

Great Eastern Conventions, Inc.
Entertainment company that produced comic book conventions, most actively during 1987-1996, and ran shows in New York City and several U.S. states.

comic book conventions

Creation Conventions

Michael Carbonaro
Promoter whose annual Big Apple Comic Con was established in 1996.

Big Apple Comic Con

Jacob K. Javits Convention Center

Esma Sultan Mansion
Historical yalı (waterside mansion) located at the Bosphorus in the Ortaköy neighborhood of Istanbul, Turkey, named after its original owner Esma Sultan, and used today as a cultural center after being redeveloped.

Bosphorus
Location at which the Esma Sultan Mansion is located.

Ortaköy
Neighborhood of Istanbul where the Esma Sultan Mansion is located.

Istanbul
City in Turkey containing the Ortaköy neighborhood.

Turkey

cultural center

yalı
Turkish term for a waterside mansion; the Esma Sultan Mansion is described as a historical yalı.

Esma Sultan Yalısı
Turkish name of the Esma Sultan Mansion.

Lanre Dabiri
Born May 23, 1977; better known by stage name Eldee, stylized as eLDee; described as a former Nigerian-American rapper, singer, and record producer, now an IT Consultant based in the United_States; 'Lanre' is a diminutive for the Yoruba name 'Olanrewaju'.

Eldee
Stage name of Lanre Dabiri, stylized as eLDee; has a master's degree in Architecture from the University of Lagos, Nigeria; original member of the band Trybesmen; hails from Lagos Island in Lagos State, Nigeria.

May 23, 1977

United_States

rapper

singer

record producer

Yoruba

Olanrewaju

Lanre

Architecture

Nigerian university from which eLDee has a master's degree in Architecture.

Nigeria

Trybesmen

Lagos Island

Hallelujah! I'm a Bum
Seventh studio album by Chicago-based rock band Local H; a concept album based on politics in the United States; completed in spring 2012 and chosen for release in September to be closer to the 2012 presidential election; makes frequent use of El Train sounds in Chicago to transition songs.

Local H
Chicago-based rock band whose seventh studio album is Hallelujah! I'm a Bum; the band chose to release the album in September.

Chicago
City where Local H is based and where the El Train whose sounds are used on the album is located.

concept album
Type of album that Hallelujah! I'm a Bum is said to be, based on politics in the United States.

politics in the United States
Subject on which the concept album Hallelujah! I'm a Bum is based.

spring of 2012
Time when Hallelujah! I'm a Bum was completed, before its September release.

September
Month when the band chose to release Hallelujah! I'm a Bum, to be closer to the 2012 presidential election.

2012 presidential election
Election the band sought to be closer to by choosing a September release for the album.

El Train
Train in Chicago whose sounds the album makes frequent use of to transition songs.

Abdülaziz
32nd Ottoman Sultan; husband of Gevheri Kadın.

Şehzade Mehmed Seyfeddin

Ottoman Empire
Empire referenced in relation to Esma Sultan.

Left Behind: The Kids

Jenkins, Tim LaHaye, and Chris Fabry; consists of 40 short novels aimed primarily at the young adult market; follows teenagers experiencing the rapture and tribulation, based on Bible scriptures and background plots from the adult Left Behind novels; published by Tyndale House Publishing from 1997 to 2004; has sold over 11 million copies worldwide.

Charles Craft
Charles Craft (May 9, 1902 – September 19, 1968) was an English-born American film and television editor; he was born in Hampshire, England, entered the Hollywood film industry in 1927, edited 90 feature-length films over 25 years, moved into television in the early 1950s, retired in 1966, and died in Los Angeles, California.

Hampshire
County in England where Craft was born on May 9, 1902.

England
Country where Craft was born; he was born in Hampshire, England.

film industry
Industry Craft entered in Hollywood in 1927.

Universal Pictures
Studio associated with the silent film Painting the Town, the first film Craft edited.

Painting the Town
Universal Pictures silent film; the first film Craft edited.

Racket Squad
Show from 1951–53 for which Craft was the main editor, editing 93 of the 98 episodes.

Meet Corliss Archer
1954 series Craft worked on.

Science Fiction Theatre
1955–56 series Craft worked on.

Highway Patrol
1955–57 series Craft worked on.

Sea Hunt
Late 1950s and early 1960s series starring Lloyd Bridges; Craft was one of its main editors, editing over half of the episodes.

Lloyd Bridges
Star of Sea Hunt.

Flipper's New Adventure
1964 film and sequel to 1963's Flipper; Craft's final film work as editor.

Flipper
1963 film to which Flipper's New Adventure is the sequel.

television series
A television series made from the film; Craft began editing duties on it, editing the first 28 episodes before he retired in 1966.

Los Angeles
City in California where Craft died on September 19, 1968.

feature-length films

Ed Wood (film)
Ed Wood is a 1994 American biographical period comedy-drama film directed and produced by Tim Burton; it stars Johnny Depp as cult filmmaker Ed Wood and concerns a period in Wood's life and his relationship with Bela Lugosi; its supporting cast includes Sarah Jessica Parker, Patricia Arquette, Jeffrey Jones, Lisa Marie, and Bill Murray.

Piano Girl
2009 Turkish comedy-drama film directed by Murat Saraçoğlu and starring Tarık Akan and Şerif Sezer as two elderly people forced to question their histories and reveal their big secrets; its Turkish title is Deli Deli Olma. It went on nationwide general release across Turkey on 17, 2009, was the opening film at the Sinema Burada Film Festival in İzmir, Turkey, and was screened in competition at the 46th Antalya Golden Orange Film Festival.
